bib.title: Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition

read.skipped: Reference list and author biographies only skimmed. Figure 9 (bar chart of error rates per classifier) is an image, so only the numbers the text prints were recorded.

question: Can pattern recognition systems be built by relying more on learning and less on hand-designed heuristics, both for isolated character recognition (convolutional nets on pixels) and for multi-module document systems (globally trained graph transformer networks)?
hypothesis: Better pattern recognition systems can be built by relying more on automatic learning and less on hand-designed heuristics; convolutional nets should beat other classifiers on 2-D shapes and global training of whole systems should beat separately trained modules.
contributions: Comparison of many classifiers on the MNIST handwritten digit task, with convolutional nets (LeNet-5, boosted LeNet-4) best
LeNet-5 architecture and its stochastic diagonal Levenberg-Marquardt training
Graph transformer networks (GTN): multi-module systems passing graphs, trained globally by gradient back-propagation
Viterbi, discriminative Viterbi, forward and discriminative forward training criteria for string-level training
Space displacement neural network (SDNN) that scans a convolutional net over the input to avoid explicit segmentation
Generalized graph composition (transduction) with check/fprop/bprop methods
Online handwriting recognizer (AMAP input + convolutional net + GTN) and a commercially deployed check reading system

method.summary: LeNet-5 (7 layers, ~60 000 free parameters) is trained with stochastic diagonal Levenberg-Marquardt on the 60 000-image MNIST training set and compared with linear, k-NN, PCA+polynomial, RBF, MLP, LeNet-1/4, boosted LeNet-4, tangent distance and SVM classifiers. The second half builds GTNs trained with a discriminative forward loss for online handwriting recognition and bank check reading.
method.task: handwritten digit classification (MNIST); word-level online handwriting recognition; bank check amount reading

datasets.name: MNIST (modified NIST)
datasets.size: 60 000 training patterns; 10 000 test images used (60 000 test set built, 5 000 from SD-1 and 5 000 from SD-3 used)
datasets.split: Training: first 250 SD-1 writers (~30 000 images) plus SD-3 from pattern #0 to reach 60 000. Test: remaining 250 SD-1 writers plus SD-3 from pattern #35 000 to reach 60 000; 10 000 used
datasets.source: NIST Special Database 3 and Special Database 1; SD-1 has 58 527 images by 500 writers
datasets.preprocessing: Bilevel images size-normalized into a 20x20 box keeping aspect ratio (anti-aliased grey levels). Regular: centered by centre of mass in 28x28 (padded to 32x32 for LeNet-5). Deslanted: sheared by second moments, cropped to 20x20. Third version 16x16 used in early experiments. LeNet-5 input pixels scaled so background -0.1 and foreground 1.175 (mean ~0, variance ~1).

models.name: LeNet-5
models.architecture: Convolutional net, 7 layers excluding input: C1 6 maps 28x28 (5x5, 156 params, 122 304 connections); S2 6 maps 14x14 (12 params, 5880 conn); C3 16 maps 10x10 (5x5, partial connection table, 1516 params, 156 000 conn); S4 16 maps 5x5 (32 params, 2000 conn); C5 120 maps 1x1 (48 120 conn); F6 84 units (10 164 params); output 10 Euclidean RBF units with fixed +-1 7x12-bitmap target codes. Squashing f(a)=A tanh(Sa), A=1.7159. Subsampling = sum of 2x2, times trainable coefficient, plus bias, then sigmoid.

models.name: LeNet-4
models.architecture: 4 first-level maps, 8 subsampling maps, 16 maps, 16 subsampling maps, fully connected 120 units, 10 outputs

models.name: LeNet-1
models.params: about 2600 free parameters; about 100 000 multiply/add steps
models.architecture: small convolutional net on 16x16 images centered in 28x28 input

models.name: Boosted LeNet-4
models.architecture: Drucker et al boosting: net 2 trained on 50% patterns net 1 got right and 50% wrong; net 3 on patterns where nets 1 and 2 disagree; outputs summed at test

models.name: Fully connected nets, linear, pairwise linear, k-NN, PCA+poly, RBF, tangent distance, SVM
models.params: linear 7850 (regular) / 4010 (deslanted) free parameters; PCA+2nd-degree polynomial on 40 components (821 inputs); RBF 1000 Gaussian units; MLPs 28x28-300-10, 28x28-1000-10, 28x28-300-100-10, 28x28-1000-150-10; pairwise linear 45 units

models.name: Online handwriting convolutional net
models.architecture: 5 layers: conv 8 kernels 3x3; 2x2 subsampling; conv 25 kernels 5x5; conv 84 kernels 4x4; 2x1 subsampling; 95 adaptive RBF output units. Input AMAP 5 planes x 20 rows x 18 columns (5-element feature vector per pixel: 4 orientations + curvature).
models.context: AMAP 5x20x18 (HOS); width varies with word for SDNN

training.objective: LeNet-5: MAP-style discriminative criterion (eq. 9) with RBF outputs (MSE criterion eq. 8 discussed); GTN systems: discriminative forward loss (constrained forward penalty minus unconstrained forward penalty)
training.optimizer: Stochastic diagonal Levenberg-Marquardt: per-parameter step size eps_k = eta / (mu + h_kk), update after each single pattern, patterns in constant random order
training.lr: global eta schedule 0.0005 (first 2 passes), 0.0002 (next 3), 0.0001 (next 3), 0.00005 (next 4), 0.00001 thereafter; mu = 0.02; effective rates in first pass between approx 7 x 10^-? (exponent lost in text extraction) and 0.016
training.epochs: 20 passes through the 60 000 training patterns per session (also stated: training set typically repeated 20 times)
training.regularisation: No explicit regulariser; weight sharing; large-learning-rate SGD argued to favour broad minima; data augmentation by distortion
training.hardware: Silicon Graphics Origin 2000 server, single 200 MHz R10000 processor
training.wall_clock: two-three days of CPU to train LeNet-5 (10-20 passes)

other.hessian_estimate: diagonal Gauss-Newton second derivatives re-estimated on 500 patterns before each pass and held fixed during the pass
other.convergence: test error stabilises after about 10-12 passes; no overtraining observed
other.SDNN_training_data: centre character plus two random side characters, gap 1-4 pixels between bounding boxes, some with no centre character (blank class), 10% salt-and-pepper noise
other.noise_robust_model: MNIST training set with each pixel inverted with probability 0.1
other.online_handwriting_phases: Phase 1: RBF centers fixed, net trained on isolated characters to minimise output distance of correct-class RBF. Phase 2: all weights and RBF centers trained globally with discriminative forward loss at word level, using stochastic diagonal LM
other.check_system: recognizer trained on 500 000 character images, then on automatically segmented truthed images, then a small subset of parameters trained globally at field level on whole check images

inference.decoding: String recognition: Viterbi (min-penalty path) or beam search over interpretation graph composed with a dictionary/grammar graph; digit classification: lowest RBF penalty
inference.samples: single run per configuration; no seeds or repeats reported

limits: Single train/test split, one run per configuration, no seeds, and no significance test; the authors quote about 0.1% uncertainty on error rates.
SVM and several other numbers come from other groups, partly by personal communication, and are not reproduced.
Fig. 9 (full per-classifier error chart) is an image, so only text-stated values were recorded.
Authors concede SDNN 'so far it has not yielded better results than HOS'.
Global training mattered only slightly in the check task because only a small subset of parameters was trained globally.
Authors say why gradient descent works with so many parameters is 'somewhat of a mystery'; their self-regularization and broad-minima explanations are conjectures.
Several hyperparameters of the online and check systems (network size, epochs, learning rates, check test set composition) are not stated.
Deployed check system details are limited; machine-print test only for the new system.
The 2-3 day CPU training time and 200 MHz R10000 hardware are of 1998 vintage; stochastic diagonal LM has since been displaced by plain SGD variants and adaptive optimizers.
Tanh/RBF output with fixed ASCII-bitmap codes and MSE-like loss were later replaced by softmax cross-entropy; not discussed here.

terms.definition: a set of units whose weights are constrained to be identical
Graph transformer network: a network of modules (graph transformers) that take one or more graphs as input and produce graphs whose arcs carry numerical information
Space displacement neural network, a convolutional network replicated over a wide input field
Heuristic oversegmentation: generate many candidate cuts by heuristics and choose the best combination using recognizer scores
loss = forward penalty of the constrained (correct-label) graph minus forward penalty of the whole interpretation graph
per-parameter learning rate computed before each pass from a diagonal Gauss-Newton Hessian estimate, with safety constant mu
annotated image where each pixel is a five-element feature vector (four pen-trajectory orientations plus curvature)
